controls.info: How the four operators connect: an arrow means the upper operator's output is added to the lower one's phase; the operators on the bottom line are heard. Click one to choose it (structural: the device recompiles, crossfaded while it plays; the circuit shows only the chosen wires).

Switches D's feedback loop on: D modulates its own phase with its output from one sample before (structural: off, D's chain runs block-wise instead of sample by sample, about a quarter of the device's cost).

controls.label: Amount
controls.info: How much of D's output (from one sample before) is added to its own phase (D is the top operator in every algorithm).

controls.label: Quality
controls.info: HQ runs the four operators at twice the sample rate and decimates their sum: FM sidebands up to 2·sr − 20 kHz no longer fold into the audible band (structural; about twice the cost).

control.info: Operator {i}'s wavetable: the wave its phase reads (a sine by default). Draw it, pick a shape, paint its harmonics along the top, add keyframes on the right; fold, warp and sync below.
Operator {i}'s phase accumulator: left arc a frequency added in Hz (0 = the ratio exactly), bottom arc the start phase, right arc the amplitude (a phase multiplier: whole numbers are harmonics).

control.label: Ratio
control.info: Operator {i} plays the note's frequency × Ratio ÷ the box below: an exact just ratio (3 ÷ 2 a fifth, 7 ÷ 4 a harmonic seventh). 0: it stops following the note, and its accumulator's frequency arc is a fixed frequency.
Divides operator {i}'s ratio (exact: two whole numbers).
Operator {i}'s envelope, a VCA on its wave: its amount is the operator's level (a carrier's loudness, a modulator's depth: amount 1 moves the phase it modulates by ±1 cycle).
